title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput benchmarks after last config changes, discuss continuous batching and target concurrency, noise observed from long tails, and agree next steps for a throughput-focused pilot run. Redwood SE suggested queue-size cap and tweak to batching window; Novapay to run 12-hour steady-state benchmark and share logs.
action_items: Daniel Kim - update batching config (max_batch_size=64, batching_window_ms=12) and upload sample config - Due: 2027-07-30
Liam O'Connor - run 12-hour steady-state throughput run on dedicated infra and share perf logs (p50/p95/p99, GPU util, KV hit-rate) - Due: 2027-08-03
Sara Bell - validate SLOs for queueing time and confirm we can accept 200ms tail increase during bursts - Due: 2027-08-02
Maya Patel - send updated pricing and pilot terms for a dedicated capacity pilot (4-week) - Due: 2027-07-29
next_steps: Redwood to provide tuned config and a short runbook for running steady-state benchmark
Novapay to run benchmark and share metrics + raw logs in shared folder
Schedule follow-up deep-dive (SE-led) after benchmark completes to review traces and adjust queuing policy
transcript:
Header: 2027-07-28 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48 mins | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Liam (Novapay Head of ML), Sara (Novapay SRE), Rohit (Novapay Eng Mgr), Aisha (Data Eng)

[00:00] Maya: Hey all, good to see everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick agenda — throughput results, continuous batching tweaks, concurrency targets, queueing policy, and then next steps.
[00:18] Liam: Yep sounds good. We ran the last pass overnight after Daniel's changes, some numbers came back but there was a weird tail at p99.
[00:27] Daniel: Yeah I saw that — looks like when we bumped the concurrency the batching window got a bit noisy, so we saw more small batches and some jitter.
[00:36] Sara: Is that the same config you recommended last week? I thought we had max_batch_size 128?
[00:41] Daniel: We moved it down for the experiment to 64 but with a slightly larger window, oh wait maybe I miscommunicated, sorry — the run we looked at had 32/20ms which probably caused extra small batches.
[00:55] Maya: No problem, that's exactly why we're here, get on the same page. Liam, do you have the p50/p95/p99 numbers you can share?
[01:05] Liam: Sure. p50 was about 45ms on tokens, p95 ~210ms, p99 spiked to 1.4s during bursts. GPU util stayed around 67% average but spiky. KV cache hit-rate was lower than expected, around 38%.
[01:20] Priya: Noted — lower cache hits will definitely push more compute. Any idea why cache wasn't hitting?
[01:25] Aisha: We instrumented prefix distribution — lots of short unique prompts, so no good reuse. Also some tokenizer differences between our preprocessing and the model that caused some mismatch.
[01:36] Rohit: That tokenizer mismatch we thought was fixed — maybe a different tokenization library on the test job, we'll double-check.
[01:42] Daniel: Two immediate levers: increase effective batching (larger batching_window_ms) to capture more requests in the same batch, or increase concurrency but cap queue size so queuing time doesn't blow up. There's tradeoffs.
[01:55] Sara: What's the recommended cap? We can't let queueing push request latency past 500ms for our core payments flows.
[02:02] Daniel: Right. For your traffic shape my suggestion is target concurrency 12-16 per model worker, max_queue_ms 200-250ms, and batching_window 10-15ms with max_batch_size 64. That gives higher GPU utilization while bounding queuing.
[02:18] Liam: If we pick concurrency 16 we saw GPU util jump to ~85% but p99 got worse.
[02:25] Daniel: The p99 increase is expected if you don't cap queueing — the long tail is due to a few requests waiting for a batch to fill. Cap the queue and they'll get routed to fallback or rejected per policy, or you provision extra capacity.
[02:36] Maya: Quick question — if we set fallback to a lower-cost model during full queue, are we okay with some degraded quality for certain endpoints?
[02:44] Liam: For some internal features yes, but not for transaction-critical flows. We'll need route-level policies.
[02:50] Daniel: We can set per-route policies, e.g., route A -> strict SLO, no fallback; route B -> allow fallback to smaller quantized model.
[02:58] Rohit: About the batching window — does increasing it hurt latency for single-user small requests? Our user-facing endpoints are sensitive.
[03:05] Daniel: It can add the batching_window ms as extra latency, but if you keep it 10-15ms it's typically imperceptible at p50. The tradeoff is better throughput and cost.
[03:15] Priya: Also remember the prefix/KV cache — if we can increase cache hit-rate we reduce compute significantly. Any quick wins there?
[03:22] Aisha: We're going to normalize tokenization and add a light canonicalization layer for common prefixes. That should push hit-rate up.
[03:29] Liam: Ok we'll try that.
[03:31] --- transcript continues with periodic checks and interruptions ---
[06:00] Maya: Daniel, you mentioned a batching window change last night that improved throughput but introduced jitter — can you walk through the exact config you pushed?
[06:09] Daniel: Sure — last night I pushed max_batch_size 64, batching_window_ms 12, concurrency target 14, and max_queue_ms 250. On paper that should smooth small bursts; however, the test harness had a small driver bug where keep-alive wasn't reusing connections so we had extra cold starts.
[06:28] Liam: Oh that explains the cold-start spikes. We saw some 200-400ms spikes unrelated to GPU.
[06:34] Sara: Connection reuse fix should help. We'll patch the harness.
[06:37] Daniel: Also we instrumented KV eviction rates — some backend TTLs were too aggressive so entries were being evicted before reuse. Increasing TTL for predictable prefixes pushed hit-rate up in the lab.
[06:50] Aisha: We'll adjust TTLs.
[06:52] Maya: Great. On the question of target concurrency, do we think 14 is the sweet spot for your current instance size?
[06:58] Daniel: For the 8xA100 instance you have in the pilot 12-16 is reasonable; I lean 14 as a balanced point. If you can run steady-state with higher concurrency we can evaluate cost-per-token vs p99 tradeoff.
[07:12] Liam: Let's plan a 12-hour steady-state run at concurrency 14 with the new batching window and TTLs. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, GPU util, queue times, and xla/kernels breakdown.
[07:23] Daniel: Perfect. Also we'll provide a short runbook and the JSON config for the runtime so it's reproducible.
[07:28] Priya: I'll attach the config to the shared folder after the call.
[07:31] --- minor crosstalk, someone drops audio for a few seconds ---
[15:10] Rohit: One thing we ran into — our burst pattern is very spiky during payroll cutoffs; we need a plan for those 10-15 minute spikes. Autoscaling takes a few minutes to add capacity.
[15:21] Daniel: For that pattern, smart routing helps: route critical traffic to reserved capacity during known windows, and use burst capacity or fallback otherwise. Also consider pre-warming and a short ramp-up window.
[15:33] Sara: What's the overhead of keeping a small reserved pool on standby?
[15:36] Maya: Pricing is in the pilot doc — small reserved pool can be cost-effective compared to SLA risk. I'll resend a one-page cost example after the call.
[15:45] Liam: Please do.
[15:47] Daniel: Another idea — progressive batching where high-priority intra-burst requests get prioritized into earlier batches, lower-priority get best-effort batching.
[15:57] Aisha: That would be great. Is that supported today?
[16:01] Daniel: We have priority queues in the runtime; you can set priority per route. The runtime will attempt to include high-priority in the first batch windows.
[16:10] Rohit: We need to validate behavior under failure — if a worker OOMs or a preemption happens, how do requests get handled?
[16:18] Daniel: The runtime retries at the routing layer and has automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We'll show you traces in the deep-dive next week.
[16:26] Maya: Ok let's talk about next steps and owners. We've already captured some action items. Anything else?
[16:33] Liam: We'll run the 12-hour benchmark (concurrency 14) and attach logs. If p99 still high, we may ask for a short A/B comparing concurrency 12 vs 16.
[16:43] Daniel: Sounds good. If you can share traces around the 1.4s p99 events that helps us diagnose batching vs kernel stalls.
[16:51] Sara: We'll include traces.
[16:53] Priya: I'll also share a quick checklist for running the steady-state run — steps to ensure connection reuse and TTLs.
[16:59] Maya: Great. Anything on security/compliance side this week?
[17:03] Liam: No changes, we already have SOC2 docs; one ask is more granularity in audit logs for model version usage — can that be surfaced?
[17:12] Maya: Yes, we can provide per-request model version and route in audit logs; I'll follow up with product on retention defaults.
[17:19] Rohit: And one last tiny ask — can we get per-token cost projection based on these throughput numbers?
[17:24] Maya: Yes, I'll send updated pricing for the pilot.
[17:27] --- wrap up ---
[17:40] Maya: Ok, thanks everyone. Recap — Redwood to push config and runbook, Novapay to run 12-hour steady-state with concurrency 14, send logs/traces, patch harness, and we'll reconvene after results.
[17:52] Liam: Thanks, talk soon.
[17:55] Daniel: Thanks all.
